papers.title: Recovering Resting-State EEG During AM-tACS Using Dynamic Adaptive Stimulation Artifact Source Separation.
papers.abstract: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) can modulate brain oscillations in a frequency-specific manner, but strong stimulation artifacts severely contaminate concurrent electroencephalography (EEG), limiting direct assessment of ongoing neural activity. Conventional artifact suppression methods often lack adaptability to nonstationary and frequency-dependent artifacts, which may cause incomplete artifact removal and neural signal distortion. This study aimed to develop a dynamic adaptive stimulation artifact source separation framework to improve EEG recovery during amplitude-modulated tACS (AM-tACS). We proposed a dynamic adaptive stimulation artifact source separation framework, termed DASASS, integrating recursive covariance updating, adaptive component selection, and wavelet-based multiband processing. This framework was designed to suppress time-varying and frequency-dependent stimulation artifacts while preserving the spectrotemporal and spatial characteristics of neural signals. The method was evaluated on resting-state EEG recorded during AM-tACS and compared with stimulation artifact source separation (SASS), principal component analysis (PCA), independent component analysis (ICA), and adaptive noise cancellation (ANC). Performance was assessed using normalized root mean square error, band-power deviation, and demodulated residual modulation. Microstate analysis examined whether recovered EEG preserved canonical spatial topographies and temporal dynamics. DASASS achieved the lowest NRMSE, shift-averaged NRMSE, and demodulated residual modulation among the tested methods, indicating improved waveform reconstruction and effective suppression of residual modulation artifacts, while its small negative band-power deviation suggested mild conservative attenuation rather than superior spectral preservation. Further microstate analysis showed that EEG recovered by DASASS preserved the four canonical microstate topographies, with spatial correlation coefficients ranging from 0.8643 to 0.9412 relative to the artifact-free reference EEG, while maintaining overall microstate temporal dynamics. These findings indicate that DASASS provides an effective solution for EEG recovery during AM-tACS. The proposed framework may support stimulation-state brain activity analysis and future closed-loop neuromodulation applications.

papers.title: Integrating wavelet signal processing and machine learning for EEG-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.
papers.abstract: BackgroundBrain diseases pose a significant global health challenge, and their diagnosis often relies on subjective clinical assessments.ObjectiveTo this end, this study proposes an integrated wavelet signal processing and machine learning framework for single-channel Electroencephalography (EEG)-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.MethodsFirst, EEG signals are decomposed into rhythm-specific sub-bands using the Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform (DWPT). Then, for each rhythm, a multi-dimensional feature matrix (MFM) is constructed by integrating Approximate Entropy (AE), Rhythm Energy Ratio (RER), C0-complexity (C0), and Zero-crossing Rate (ZCR), which comprehensively models the EEG characteristics. Six classifiers were compared under subject-level leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, and Decision Tree (DT) was selected as the representative classifier. Each channel was then evaluated independently as a complete single-channel system, and representative channels were identified from the completed results.ResultsValidated on publicly available datasets for SCHIZ (schizophrenia), UNM (Parkinson's disease), and MPHCE (depression), the method achieves impressive accuracies of 84.52% (F4), 86.54% (F4), and 93.10% (Fp1), respectively, using single-channel EEG electrode.ConclusionsSuch results demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains robust detection performance in each of the three disease-specific tasks. The framework is lightweight by design, using only a single EEG channel and a single simple machine-learning model for classification. It needs no multi-channel feature concatenation or decision-level fusion. This single-channel design suits hardware and data sources with limited resources, and may support the development of low-cost portable EEG systems.

papers.title: Forecasting Next-Day Alcohol Craving in Individuals With Problematic Alcohol Use With Multimodal Data and a Tiny Recurrent Neural Network: Prospective Longitudinal Study.
papers.abstract: Alcohol craving is associated with drinking behaviors despite negative consequences and relapse following periods of abstinence or treatment. Accurately forecasting alcohol craving is crucial for preventing alcohol consumption and relapse, thereby mitigating alcohol-related problems. Previous studies have assessed alcohol craving using diverse modalities such as psychological assessments, neurophysiological measures including electroencephalography (EEG) or heart rate variability (HRV) at a single time point, and digital phenotypes collected longitudinally via smartphone apps. However, alcohol craving is inherently heterogeneous and multidimensional across individuals and over time, making it difficult to capture using any single modality alone. In contrast, multimodal AI enables the prediction of alcohol craving by integrating complementary behavioral and neurophysiological features. This study aimed to develop and evaluate AI models to forecast next-day alcohol craving in individuals with problematic alcohol use with multimodal datasets. We analyzed multimodal datasets comprising smartphone-based digital phenotypes collected over 28 days, along with baseline EEG, HRV, and psychological measures in a prospective longitudinal study of 60 participants with problematic alcohol use. A tiny multimodal recurrent neural network (RNN) was implemented, in which representations of static baseline features were encoded into a latent representation and used to initialize the hidden state of the RNN. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, weighted F1-score, macro F1-score, and mean absolute error (MAE). The multimodal model consistently outperformed the unimodal model based on digital phenotypes alone, achieving higher accuracy (0.56 vs 0.45), weighted F1-score (0.51 vs 0.38), and macro F1-score (0.37 vs 0.24), along with lower MAE (0.68 vs 0.90). At the individual level, 72% (43/60) of participants showed improved prediction accuracy with the multimodal model. These improvements were statistically significant (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P<.001; paired t test, P<.001). Integrating digital phenotypes with neurophysiological and psychological features enhances the prediction of short-term alcohol craving dynamics. This approach may enable more precise and timely personalized interventions for individuals at risk of relapse.

The multimodal model outperformed the digital-phenotype-only model (accuracy 0.56 vs 0.45; MAE 0.68 vs 0.90), with improved accuracy in 72% of participants.

papers.title: Next generation Human Neocortical Neurosolver model with biophysically realistic somatic, dendritic and synaptic dynamics
papers.abstract: The Human Neocortical Neurosolver (HNN) is an open-source biophysical modeling tool for multiscale interpretation of human electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) signals. HNN's foundation is a pre-tuned canonical neocortical circuit model consisting of excitatory pyramidal neurons and inhibitory interneurons in supra- (L2/3) and infragranular (L5) layers. This model was originally developed based on studies in rodent and non-human primate cortices when dynamics of human neurons were poorly characterized. Yet recent advances in recordings from human tissue now provide unprecedented detail to update the model. Here, we present a significantly updated model for use in the HNN software, with electrophysiological properties and synaptic connections tuned to human tissue. Beyond reproducing biologically realistic somatic dynamics, the pyramidal cells simulate dendritic calcium (Ca2+) spikes in the L5 extratelencephalic-projecting (ET) neurons, and shorter dendritic spikes in the L2/3 pyramidal neurons. We demonstrate how the updated circuitry and new features in the HNN software can be used to disentangle somatic, synaptic, and dendritic contributions to human E-/MEG signatures. The model is distributed with workflows to simulate event-related responses and oscillations, and tutorials demonstrating how membrane potentials, Ca2+ dynamics, and synaptic currents can be recorded and visualized. These enhancements allow extensive model validations based on in vitro and in vivo electrophysiology, voltage and Ca2+ imaging, and provide users with novel insights on the mechanisms underlying E-/MEG signals.

papers.title: Cross-cohort validation of EEG biomarkers using a pre-registered three-criterion framework: a demonstration in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
papers.abstract: Background. Despite decades of EEG biomarker development for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), no candidate has progressed to clinical deployment, partly because cross-cohort validation is rare. We aimed to develop and demonstrate a pre-registered three-criterion screening framework to identify which candidate EEG features show the combined properties required for biomarker translation: cross-sectional discrimination, within-subject reliability, and cross-cohort effect consistency. Methods. We pre-registered a validation framework adapted from FDA-NIH BEST principles and applied it to 18 EEG features across three independent cohorts: EEGET-ALS (six ALS patients, 170 healthy controls; home recordings over 17 days), UCL/Penn State (eight ALS patients; clinic recordings over 1-2 months), and a healthy adult test-retest reference (60 participants, three sessions over one month). Features were required to meet three pre-registered criteria: (1) cross-sectional discrimination (Cohen's d > 0.5), (2) within-subject reliability (ICC(3,1) > 0.6 in both ALS cohorts independently), and (3) cross-cohort effect direction consistency. Cross-cohort permutation testing (1000 iterations) and subject-level bootstrap resampling (500 iterations) were applied to assess robustness. Results. Three features met all three pre-registered criteria: gamma power, theta power, and spectral entropy. Cross-cohort permutation testing showed that no permutation, out of 1000, produced any feature in the three-cohort reliability intersection (Monte Carlo p = 0.001). Bootstrap resampling indicated that the composition of the selected set was sensitive to sample composition (median count 1, 95% CI [0, 4]), with gamma power (67% inclusion), spectral entropy (43%), and theta power (32%) the most stable features at a relaxed reliability threshold (ICC > 0.5); at the primary pre-registered threshold (ICC > 0.6), the corresponding inclusion probabilities are lower (57%, 27%, and 19%, respectively). A principal methodological finding was that cross-cohort differences in feature reliability were large relative to the apparent disease-associated signal, most clearly demonstrated by relative beta power (ICC = 0.09 in a home-recorded cohort versus 0.93 in a clinic-recorded cohort); because recording protocol, hardware, setting, population, and preprocessing all differ jointly between cohorts in this dataset, this is evidence of cohort-associated variability that plausibly includes a protocol contribution, not a separately identified, isolated protocol effect. Conclusions. This study provides a pre-registered, multi-cohort EEG biomarker screening framework for ALS with explicit bootstrap-quantified uncertainty. Gamma power, spectral entropy, and theta power are identified as priority candidates for prospective validation. A recurring methodological observation is that protocol-related cohort differences appear to contribute more to cross-cohort variability than disease-related effects within this dataset; because protocol is confounded with cohort, equipment, and preprocessing, this pattern is descriptive rather than causal. The observation nonetheless has direct implications for the design of multi-site EEG biomarker studies in neural engineering.

ai.reason: Pre-registered three-criterion validation with test-retest reliability and cross-cohort consistency, directly relevant to reproducibility and adaptable biomarker pipelines.
ai.summary: Applied a pre-registered three-criterion framework (cross-sectional discrimination, within-subject reliability, cross-cohort effect consistency) to screen 18 EEG features for ALS biomarkers across three independent cohorts. Gamma power, theta power, and spectral entropy met all criteria, while cross-cohort reliability differences (e.g., relative beta power ICC 0.09 vs 0.93) were large relative to disease-associated signal and bootstrap analyses showed selected-set sensitivity to sample composition.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG spectral characteristics before and after a single auditory integration training session in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.abstract: Resting-state EEG characteristics may differ between autistic and non-autistic children. Conventional band power mixes periodic and broadband activity; spectral parameterization separates periodic peaks from the aperiodic background. Auditory integration training (AIT) is used as a complementary intervention, but its immediate neurophysiological and clinical effects remain uncertain. We examined baseline EEG differences and pre-post changes around one AIT session. Twenty children with ASD and 15 typically developing (TD) children aged 6-8 years participated. Resting EEG was recorded in ASD before and immediately after a 30-min Berard AIT session. Sixteen ASD participants had usable paired recordings. Relative power was measured in five bands. Periodic and aperiodic components were parameterized with FOOOF. Sensitivity analyses varied R-squared threshold, aperiodic mode, fitting settings, channel aggregation. At baseline, ASD showed higher delta and lower theta, alpha, and beta relative power than TD. After modeling peaks, aperiodic exponent and offset did not differ between groups. Among 16 paired ASD recordings, delta decreased and beta/gamma increased post-session; paired tests of exponent and offset were nonsignificant. Five of 20 baseline and seven of 18 post-session recordings had R-squared<0.90, but sensitivity analyses did not change null aperiodic findings. This uncontrolled pilot study found immediate pre-post band-power differences around one Berard AIT session but no significant FOOOF-derived aperiodic changes. Findings are hypothesis-generating and cannot distinguish AIT-specific effects from repeated measurement, arousal, expectancy, or generic auditory stimulation. Variable fit quality and small sample limit precision; controlled longitudinal studies are needed.

ai.summary: Examined resting-state EEG spectral characteristics in 20 children with ASD and 15 typically developing children, and pre-post changes around a single 30-min Berard auditory integration training session using FOOOF spectral parameterization. ASD showed higher delta and lower theta/alpha/beta relative power at baseline; post-session delta decreased and beta/gamma increased, but aperiodic exponent and offset showed no significant changes.

papers.title: A shared slowing axis and phenotype-specific rhythms link clinical EEG to FDG-PET dementia phenotypes
papers.abstract: Early and accurate identification of neurodegenerative disorders has notable implications for treatment and quality of life. Whereas neuroimaging-based biomarkers can accurately identify neurodegenerative subtypes, EEG represents a low-cost alternative that could expand access to dementia care. Here, we investigated whether six data-driven EEG latent factors, derived by nonnegative tensor decomposition of clinical EEGs, differ systematically across FDG-PET-defined neurodegenerative phenotypes. In 455 patients with EEG and FDG-PET acquired within one year of each other, factor expression was compared across 14 diagnostic classes assigned by StateViewer, a validated artificial intelligence framework for FDG-PET interpretation. To separate disease-general severity from phenotype-specific topography, each factor was also regressed on a subject-level slowing index. Finally, we related the factors to regional FDG uptake and to neuropsychological performance (n = 98) and assessed their potential utility for single-subject classification. Four factors reflecting neurophysiological oscillations (posterior alpha, Rolandic beta, frontotemporal delta-theta and posterior theta-slow alpha) varied significantly across phenotypes, with attenuation of faster and augmentation of slower rhythms most pronounced in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), dysexecutive Alzheimer disease (AD) and posterior cortical atrophy, whereas factors dominated by eye-movement and muscle artifact showed no robust phenotypic association. Alpha and beta effects were largely attributable to overall slowing, whereas posterior theta-slow alpha became more phenotype-specific after adjustment (eta-squared 0.082 to 0.147), dissociating the Alzheimer disease spectrum from frontotemporal syndromes. The slowing index tracked with an FDG-PET pattern highly associated with DLB across the cohort, irrespective of assigned phenotype (r = 0.51, P < 0.001). Consistent with a model in which dementia phenotypes reflect altered hippocampal-neocortical oscillatory coupling (stochastic latent oscillatory diffusion), frontotemporal delta-theta tracked a limbocortical axis of metabolic pattern expression, rising with neocortical and falling with limbic-predominant involvement, independent of overall slowing and phenotype. Each factor mapped onto a distinct metabolic topography, with frontotemporal delta-theta resembling Alzheimer-type hypometabolism and posterior theta-slow alpha the medial occipital hypometabolism of DLB. In terms of neuropsychological performance, Rolandic beta was associated with executive functions, and frontotemporal delta-theta with memory, visuospatial and global performance. Using these four factors alone, an exploratory logistic regression classifier separated cognitively unimpaired participants from DLB, posterior cortical atrophy, typical AD, and dysexecutive AD (area under the curve > 0.8) but poorly discriminated frontotemporal dementia phenotypes canonically associated with 4-repeat tau. Thus, data-driven decomposition of clinical EEG separates oscillatory activity from artifact into factors that track metabolic phenotype, regional metabolism and cognition, capturing both overall slowing and phenotype-specific patterns. This work informs the further development of scalable, biology-informed EEG-based phenotyping of neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Source-resolved electroencephalogram microstates reveal opposing prefrontal-posterior dynamics and a candidate temporal-to-precuneus pathway in disorders of consciousness.
papers.abstract: Objective and circuit-level biomarkers of consciousness are urgently needed for disorders of consciousness. We recorded high-density electroencephalography from 33 patients with disorders of consciousness (17 vegetative state/unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, 16 minimally conscious state) and 19 healthy controls during rest and auditory stimulation, and combined source-localized microstate analysis with hypothesis-generating Granger causality analysis. Source microstate 3 (right prefrontal) and microstate 4 (parieto-occipital-temporal) showed diametrically opposite dynamics: microstate 3 was enhanced in the vegetative state whereas microstate 4 coverage and occurrence were higher in the minimally conscious state, revealing a fronto-posterior opponent imbalance. In repeated internal cross-validation within this cohort, microstate 4 occurrence discriminated the two patient groups (area under the curve = 0.812, 95% confidence interval 0.647-0.945). Hypothesis-generating connectivity analysis nominally implicated stronger right middle temporal-to-precuneus information flow in the minimally conscious state, a signal that did not survive network-level multiplicity correction. Source-resolved microstates thus reveal opposing cortical dynamics associated with consciousness level.

Hypothesis-generating Granger causality nominally implicated stronger right middle temporal-to-precuneus flow in minimally conscious state, though this did not survive network-level correction.

papers.title: Aperiodic Exponent as an EEG Marker of Interoceptive Attention during Gastric Fullness
papers.abstract: Gastric interoceptive attention to internal, bodily signals such as hunger, satiety, and fullness are important for regulating feeding behaviors. However, abnormal processing or sensitivity to these can lead to disorders that result in overly restrictive or excessive consumption, highlighting the need for better understanding of the cortical processing of these cues. Specifically, understanding cortical representations of self-perceived gastric fullness have yet to be studied in humans. In this work, we demonstrate that consistently across individuals, the broadband power spectral density of EEG signals, as quantified by the aperiodic exponent, flattens after individuals drink water until fullness. Simultaneous measures of the stomach and heart demonstrate increased vagal drive to peripheral organs. We further find that changes in cortical aperiodic exponent patterns are associated with changes in the frequency of gastric oscillations. Overall, this suggests that the EEG aperiodic exponent may be a useful noninvasive biomarker for assessing gastric interoceptive attention.

ai.summary: Showed that the EEG aperiodic exponent flattens after water intake to fullness consistently across individuals, accompanied by increased vagal drive to peripheral organs measured via simultaneous gastric and cardiac recordings. Changes in cortical aperiodic exponent patterns were associated with changes in gastric oscillation frequency, suggesting the exponent as a noninvasive biomarker of gastric interoceptive attention.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Neonatal Seizure Detection: A Pragmatic Evaluation of Clinical Performance Tradeoffs in Clinical EEG.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate how three artificial intelligence (AI)-based neonatal seizure detectors (NSDs) perform in a large, clinically acquired data set and their potential to support timely seizure identification. We conducted a secondary analysis of continuous EEG (cEEG) recordings from 169 neonates born at ≥35 weeks gestation with neonatal encephalopathy. Seizure presence was determined by independent review by two or three pediatric encephalographers, and 2,455 individual seizures were annotated by a single expert as a pragmatic, clinically representative reference standard. Three NSDs were evaluated: a feature-based support vector machine detector (NSD1) and two deep-learning detectors (NSD2 and Persyst-15). Using an any-overlap approach, outcomes included neonate-level seizure identification, seizure-level detection, false detections per day (FD/day), and detection latency. We analyzed 15,343 hours of cEEG (median 98 hours per neonate); 55 neonates (33%) had seizures. All NSDs identified ≥95% of neonates with seizures. Seizure-level detection varied: NSD2 detected 35% (IQR 17-53%), NSD1 63% (IQR 38-82%), and Persyst-15 60% (IQR 37-80%) of seizures. NSD1 generated significantly more FDs (46 FD/day, IQR 22-82) than NSD2 (3.2 IQR 1.2-9.3) and Persyst-15 (2.8 IQR 1.1-6.2; P < 0.0001). The median time to first true detection was <1 minute for NSD1 and Persyst-15, versus 26 minutes for NSD2. AI-based NSDs demonstrated high infant-level sensitivity but different tradeoffs between seizure-level detection and alarm burden. These findings highlight how AI tools may augment clinical EEG workflows and support earlier seizure recognition, while underscoring the need for evaluation under real-world conditions to guide safe and effective implementation.

ai.summary: Evaluated three AI-based neonatal seizure detectors on 15,343 hours of continuous EEG from 169 neonates with encephalopathy, finding all identified ≥95% of seizure-positive infants but with differing tradeoffs between seizure-level detection and false alarm burden. NSD2 had the lowest false detections (3.2/day) but detected only 35% of seizures, whereas NSD1 and Persyst-15 detected 60-63% with higher false detections for NSD1 (46/day).

papers.title: A Neuroscientific Prior-Guided Multi-View Network With Structured Channel Selection for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition is important for affective human-computer interaction and computer-aided mental health monitoring. Existing deep learning methods often overlook brain spatial topology or rely on complex dynamic graphs, which may introduce volume-conduction-induced spurious correlations and limit interpretability. This paper proposes SGA-MVTN, a neuroscientific prior-guided two-stage framework integrating a Multi-View Tower Network (MVTN) for prior-constrained feature modeling and a Structured Genetic Algorithm (SGA) for topology-aware channel selection. Specifically, MVTN keeps anatomically defined spatial views and frequency-band-specific spectral views separate until fusion, while SGA embeds functional grouping and hemispheric symmetry priors into evolutionary operators. Unlike spatial-spectral models operating on a fixed electrode set, the proposed framework connects view-specific representation learning with topology-aware electrode subset search. Under the leave-one-subject-out protocol, full-channel MVTN achieves 87.91% on SEED and 71.09% on SEED-IV. Under the channel-selection protocol, SGA-MVTN reduces the number of EEG channels by 54.84% while retaining 95.56% of the corresponding full-channel accuracy and achieves the highest accuracy among the evaluated reduced-channel methods. The separate towers also provide model-derived spatial and spectral importance estimates.

papers.title: Wearable electrophysiology monitoring enabled by stretchable porous composite conductors.
papers.abstract: We report a porous AgNWs/PEDOT:PSS composite electrode with uniform conductive networks and cold-welded junctions, fabricated by template-assisted assembly. The porous architecture effectively dissipates stress and accommodates strain, yielding excellent performance at 50% strain and stable performance over 5000 stretching cycles. The electrode enables reliable ECG, EOG, and EMG monitoring.

papers.title: In-ear electroencephalography: a systematic review of technology, applications, challenges, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used to monitor brain activity in both clinical and research settings. However, conventional scalp EEG systems require multiple electrodes, specialised equipment, and trained personnel, which limits their practicality for long-term monitoring in everyday environments. In-ear EEG has emerged as a promising wearable alternative that enables discreet and portable neural monitoring. This systematic review examines the current state of research on in-ear EEG technologies. Twenty-four studies met the inclusion criteria and were analysed thematically. The literature highlights rapid progress in device miniaturisation and wearable design, with reported applications including sleep monitoring, seizure detection, cognitive workload assessment, fatigue monitoring, and emotion recognition. Despite these advances, challenges remain related to signal quality, spatial coverage, and motion artefacts. Further research is required to validate in-ear EEG for broader clinical and real-world applications.

papers.title: Orthographic repetition elicits enhancement without suppression at both the word- and character-levels in Chinese.
papers.abstract: In Chinese, orthographic repetition (e.g., ""-"") modulates neural activity associated with orthographic processing around 200 ms after target onset, as indexed by the N200 enhancement effect. The present study combined time-frequency analysis with priming paradigms in two EEG experiments to determine whether orthographic repetition is accompanied by oscillatory power enhancement or suppression. In Experiment 1, complete repetition priming of two-character words elicited both a significant N200 enhancement effect and significant theta power enhancement relative to the control condition, whereas no significant N200 or theta-power enhancement was detected for semantic or phonological priming. To separate orthographic overlap from the concomitant phonological and semantic repetition inherent in complete repetition, Experiment 2 used partial orthographic repetition with single-character prime-target pairs that differed in phonology and semantics and replicated both effects. Exploratory participant-level correlations between the N200 and total theta effects were positive but nonsignificant in both experiments. A positive correlation between N200 enhancement and evoked theta enhancement reached the unadjusted significance threshold only in Experiment 2. These findings indicate that orthographic repetition is associated with enhancement rather than suppression of theta-band activity and that this pattern extends across word and character levels.

These findings indicate orthographic repetition produces theta-band enhancement rather than suppression across word and character levels.

papers.title: Real-World Improvement in Motor Status Among Regular Users of a Home-Based Brain-Computer Interface After Stroke
papers.abstract: BackgroundUpper extremity impairment persists in many stroke survivors, and few treatments are effective for severe chronic deficits. Brain-computer interface (BCI) therapy, which pairs decoded motor-intention-associated electrophysiology with sensory feedback, has improved upper extremity impairment in randomized trials, including in patients with severe paresis. Whether these benefits translate to routine care has rarely been evaluated. This study examined upper extremity motor recovery through 1 year among patients prescribed at-home BCI therapy in clinical practice. MethodsThis retrospective observational study included adults who were prescribed the IpsiHand System, an electroencephalography-based BCI, through a commercial US home therapy program, had a baseline Upper Extremity Fugl-Meyer (UEFM) assessment, and averaged >1 session per week through their last assessment. Occupational therapists administered the UEFM by video every 4 weeks. The primary outcome was UEFM change from baseline to week 12. A mixed model for repeated measures estimated change through week 52, with multiple imputation sensitivity analyses for missing data. ResultsOf 452 patients included in analyses (mean time since stroke, 5.4{+/-}5.4 years), mean baseline UEFM was 20.1{+/-}14.6, with 333 patients (73.7%) having severe motor impairment (UEFM 0-28). At week 12, mean UEFM change was 4.3 points (95% CI, 3.7-4.9; P<0.001), and 31.7% achieved the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 5.25 points. Mean change reached the MCID at week 16 (5.6, 95% CI [4.8, 6.4]). Model-estimated change in UEFM continued to improve through 1 year, being 6.1 (95% CI, 5.5-6.8) at week 24 and 8.1 (95% CI, 6.8-9.4) at week 52. ConclusionsAmong regular users of at-home BCI therapy in routine care, most of whom had severe chronic impairment, UEFM scores improved by 12 weeks, reached MCID by 16 weeks, and continued to increase through 1 year. At-home BCI therapy merits evaluation in randomized trials with follow-up beyond 12 weeks.

papers.title: A neural geometry for forelimb proprioception in the cervical spinal cord
papers.abstract: Precise, real-time somatosensory feedback is essential for coordinated movement, yet how the nervous system constructs a kinematic representation of the limb from this feedback is unclear. Here, using single-unit electrophysiology in the cervical spinal cords of awake and anesthetized mice, we show that spinal neurons generate a precise, ordered, low-dimensional representation of forelimb kinematic state from muscle and tendon afferent input. This representation arises from two molecularly distinct, developmentally defined classes of dorsal horn neurons. One class encodes limb speed, position and direction; the other fires phasically, with precise, radially periodic firing fields that tile kinematic space. Transient perturbation of muscle and tendon afferents in mice reaching to spatial targets causes endpoint errors predicted by deficits in the neural code. These findings show that spinal networks, one synapse removed from the periphery, are sufficient to construct a precise representation of forelimb movement.

papers.title: HRA-Former: Hierarchical Region-Aware Transformer with Structure-Preserving Multi-Stage Learning for EEG-Based Driver Fatigue Detection.
papers.abstract: Driver fatigue is associated with changes in neural rhythms and interregional coordination. However, most EEG-based fatigue detection methods model dense inter-electrode dependencies with limited attention to the electrode-to-region hierarchy. Conventional classification objectives may also favor discriminative patterns while inadequately preserving EEG spatial and spectral structure. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hierarchical region-aware Transformer with structure-preserving multi-stage learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection. The proposed framework first aggregates electrode-level features into region-level features using prototypeattention aggregation and incorporates two-dimensional scalp positional encoding to retain spatial topology. A region-aware attention mask regulates information propagation based on predefined region assignments, preserving electrode-to-region interactions and global communication among regions. Furthermore, a two-stage learning strategy is developed. In the first stage, masked EEG feature reconstruction and fatigue classification are jointly optimized to learn structure-preserving and taskrelevant representations. In the second stage, the pretrained encoder is transferred to a dedicated classifier for supervised fatigue recognition. Experiments on SEED-VIG and an independently collected dataset achieved subject-dependent accuracies of 95.18% and 86.67%, respectively, outperforming representative methods. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. These results suggest that electrode-toregion modeling enables physiologically structured EEG representations and improves fatigue detection.

papers.title: Beyond Onset Timing: Longer Sound Envelope Duration Enhances Neural Representation of the Musical Beat.
papers.abstract: Musical rhythm is often experienced with a periodic beat, serving as a temporal reference for coordinating movement. Thus far, models of beat processing have mainly relied on representing sensory inputs as patterns of onset timing, largely overlooking other acoustic features. Here, we challenge this view by showing that the internal representation of beat is affected by other temporal features of the stimulus beyond onset timing alone. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) while participants listened to rhythmic sequences designed to elicit a beat. Across conditions, we manipulated the duration of the tones conveying the rhythms, while keeping all other parameters identical, including overall intensity, speed, and rhythmic pattern structure. Beat periodicity was enhanced in the EEG responses with increased sound duration, even though it was not prominent in either the acoustic envelope or the output of a biomimetic auditory nerve model, thus pointing to higher-level processing beyond basic sensory confounds. These results demonstrate the preferential role of longer sound durations in fostering temporal scaffolding processes that integrate fast rhythmic inputs into behavior-relevant internal structures, such as the beat. More generally, our findings support a holistic processing account whereby features beyond onset timing are integrated into a neural representation of rhythm.

papers.title: A Dual-Branch Model based Federated Learning Framework for Seizure-Type Classification.
papers.abstract: Accurate seizure-type identification is of great significance for epilepsy patient treatment and management. Manual electroencephalogram (EEG) data analysis, the traditional method, is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and subjective. While deep learning has shown great potential in medical diagnosis, it faces privacy and data silo challenges in handling multi-center EEG data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-branch model and federated learning-based automatic classification method for seizure types. A federated learning framework is introduced to facilitate multi-center data collaborative training while protecting data privacy. In the base model, the one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1DCNN) and the two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2DCNN) are integrated to extract the complexity features of EEG signals and the topological features of brain networks, respectively, and the dual-modal features are adaptively integrated through the dynamic attention fusion module. In local training of federated learning framework, the FedProx optimization strategy is adopted to effectively solve the model update divergence problem caused by non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data and improve the model generalization ability. Experimental results show that the proposed federated learning framework performs well in core indicators of seizure-type classification such as accuracy and macro-average F1 score. Even in the case of extremely unbalanced data, the proposed method can still maintain an accuracy of 98.42% and a macro-average F1 score of 94.79%. This method provides an effective solution for distributed medical data collaborative training, which is of great significance for promoting the accurate diagnosis and treatment of epilepsy.

papers.title: Retrieval practice is associated with attenuated stress-related inference impairment and stronger reactivation of bridge-related category information
papers.abstract: A hallmark of human memory is its ability to form novel inferences by linking discrete but related events. We examined whether acute stress impairs memory inference and if retrieval practice can buffer this effect. Participants were trained on image pairs, AB and BC, to establish interconnected triads (ABC) with a shared bridge element B. Twenty-four hours later, we induced acute stress in half of the participants and then tested their capacity to infer the indirect AC associations. Behavioral results indicated that acute stress reduced inference accuracy and slowed responses, and retrieval practice was associated with attenuation of stress-induced impairment in A-C inference accuracy and speed. Using multivariate decoding analysis of human electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings, we found neural evidence of rapid reactivation of bridge-related category information during inference, a neural signature predictive of subsequent successful inference. Importantly, stress was associated with reduced bridge-related category reactivation, whereas retrieval practice was associated with stronger reactivation under stress. Collectively, our findings link rapid reactivation of bridge-related category information to successful memory-based inference. Although susceptible to stress, this reactivation was stronger following retrieval practice, suggesting that robust memory traces may contribute to more resilient inference under stress.

papers.title: Preclinical Pharmacology of Solriamfetol: Potential Mechanisms for Wake Promotion.
papers.abstract: Solriamfetol is a wake-promoting agent (WPA) approved for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness associated with narcolepsy and obstructive sleep apnea. The wake-promoting mechanism of solriamfetol may result from dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake inhibition. Preclinical pharmacology studies were conducted to further elucidate the molecular targets activated by solriamfetol and compare them to that of known WPAs and traditional stimulants. In vitro binding and functional studies were conducted in a panel of cell lines or membrane preparations expressing transmembrane receptors and monoamine transporters to measure the activity of solriamfetol, comparator WPAs, and traditional stimulants. Electrophysiology studies were conducted in slice preparations from mouse ventral tegmental area (VTA). Studies to measure locomotor activity and wake-promoting effects were conducted in mice. In vitro functional studies showed agonist activity of solriamfetol at human, mouse, and rat TAAR1 receptors. hTAAR1 EC50 values (10-16 μM) were within the clinically observed therapeutic solriamfetol plasma concentration range and overlapped with the observed DAT/NET inhibitory potencies of solriamfetol in vitro. TAAR1 agonist activity was unique to solriamfetol; neither the WPA modafinil nor the DAT/NET inhibitor bupropion had TAAR1 agonist activity. Solriamfetol (1-10 μM) dose-dependently inhibited the firing frequency of dopaminergic VTA neurons in mouse brain slices, similar to known TAAR1 agonists; however, these effects were inhibited by a D2 antagonist, suggesting a DAT-mediated effect. Unlike traditional stimulants, solriamfetol did not increase locomotor activity in naive mice, but inhibited the increase in locomotor activity in DAT knockout mice. Preclinical studies have identified agonist activity at the TAAR1 receptor and, possibly, lower potency agonist activity at 5-HT1A receptors as potential pharmacological targets for solriamfetol, in addition to its activity as a DAT/NET inhibitor. Given the current understanding of TAAR1 agonists as modulators of monoamine transmission with potential wake-promoting effects in multiple preclinical species, agonist activity at the hTAAR1 receptor may represent an additional pharmacological target underlying the wake-promoting effects for solriamfetol, in addition to its DNRI activity. papers.title: Healthy aging, processing speed, and mnemonic brain state engagement.
papers.abstract: Healthy older adults exhibit both selective impairments in episodic memory - memory for events situated within a specific time and place - and deficits in executive function, reflected by difficulty switching between different tasks and inhibiting task-irrelevant information. Prior work has shown that older adults show diminished mnemonic brain state engagement - recruitment of whole brain activity patterns that selectively support memory encoding and memory retrieval. Our hypothesis is that older adults are biased toward the retrieval state and, due to executive function deficits, cannot easily switch out of this state when task-irrelevant. Our goal was to determine the extent to which stimulus processing time impacts older adult mnemonic state engagement, with the expectation that longer processing times would enable older adults to switch out of a task-irrelevant retrieval state. We recorded scalp electroencephalography (EEG) while younger and older adult participants explicitly encoded and retrieved object stimuli under variable stimulus durations. Using a combination of multivariate decoding approaches, we find that under time constraints, older adults both under-recruit a young adult-like retrieval state when task-relevant, but over-recruit a participant-specific retrieval state when task-irrelevant. Older adults may thus recruit idiosyncratic activity patterns to compensate for difficulties engaging young adult-like mnemonic brain states. Taken together, these findings suggest that although older adults retain the ability to engage encoding and retrieval brain states, they require more processing time to both initiate and maintain goal-relevant mnemonic states.

papers.title: Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity after magnetic seizure therapy in treatment-resistant depression: an exploratory task-based EEG study.
papers.abstract: Magnetic seizure therapy (MST) is an emerging convulsive treatment for treatment-resistant depression (TRD) with efficacy comparable to electroconvulsive therapy and superior cognitive safety. However, its neurophysiological mechanisms-particularly those underlying conflict monitoring and response inhibition-remain unclear. Frontal midline theta-band activity indexes anterior cingulate-prefrontal cognitive-control activity and may reflect inefficient neural processing in depression. In this open-label, single-arm trial, 19 patients with TRD (16 female; mean age 20.89 ± 8.16 years; 10 of the 19 participants were minors) received 6-12 MST sessions using 100-Hz double-cone coil stimulation targeting bilateral F3/F4 frontal regions. Clinical assessments, including the 24-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-24), Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS), and 64-channel Go/Nogo task-based electroencephalography (EEG), were performed before and after treatment. EEG outcome measures included event-related potentials (N2/P3), time-frequency power (theta/beta), microstate dynamics, and theta-beta cross-frequency coupling. Following MST, patients showed significant reductions in depressive symptoms (HAMD: 40.53 ± 10.25 to 22.53 ± 11.21; MADRS: 35.68 ± 8.84 to 20.68 ± 11.12). Response rates ranged from 42.1% to 57.9%. Behavioral data could not be formally analyzed due to incomplete data storage. At an uncorrected threshold, total Nogo-related theta-band activity (4-7 Hz) at Fz and FCz was lower after treatment; however, these effects did not survive FDR correction. ERP amplitudes did not change significantly. Exploratory microstate analysis showed nominal changes in Map4 AUC during Go processing and Map2 duration during Nogo processing; none survived FDR correction. These parameters should not be interpreted as reflecting changes in neural activation or inhibitory preparation. No significant changes were observed in theta-beta cross-frequency coupling or Go-condition theta power. These preliminary findings suggest that MST was associated with short-term symptom improvement and lower total Nogo-related theta-band activity at an uncorrected threshold. Because no control group, complete behavioral data, normative comparison, Time × Condition interaction, or EEG-clinical association was available, these findings cannot establish causal mechanisms, condition specificity, improved neural efficiency, or biomarker utility. Replication in adequately powered controlled studies with complete behavioral and longitudinal clinical measures is required.

papers.title: Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Biophysical Mechanisms, Neural Effects, and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Low-intensity transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) has emerged as a promising noninvasive neuromodulation technology capable of targeting both cortical and deep brain structures with millimeter-scale spatial precision. Recent advances in ultrasound hardware, acoustic modeling, neuronavigation, and multimodal imaging have accelerated the field from proof-of-concept demonstrations toward mechanistic investigation and early clinical translation. In parallel, growing evidence from animal and human studies has begun to clarify how ultrasound influences neural activity across cellular, circuit, and systems levels. In this review, we synthesize recent progress in understanding the biophysical mechanisms, neurophysiological effects, and network-level consequences of TUS. We discuss insights from optical imaging, electrophysiology, EEG source imaging, and functional MRI, highlighting how these complementary approaches reveal cell-type-specific responses, bidirectional modulation of neural circuits, and distributed changes in functional connectivity beyond the sonicated target. We further examine evidence that functional imaging is evolving from a simple measure of regional activation to a multidimensional biomarker of target engagement, circuit modulation, and treatment response. Despite these advances, important challenges remain. We conclude that TUS is approaching a translational inflection point in which rigorous mechanistic studies, standardized methodologies, and imaging-based biomarkers can establish ultrasound as both a powerful causal neuroscience tool and a clinically viable neuromodulation therapy for disorders involving dysfunctional brain circuits.

papers.title: Comparative EEG analysis of Sutra and Tantra meditations: insights into meditative states and long-term traits.
papers.abstract: The Tibetan Buddhist tradition distinguishes between two broad categories of meditation: Sutra and Tantra, which differ in the methods and mental faculties they employ. The main neurophysiological studies of Tibetan Buddhist meditation have been conducted mostly on Sutra practices; while Tantric meditation remains less studied. This publication presents a dual comparative study, using both between-groups and within-subjects design, of the neurophysiological (EEG) correlates characterizing Sutra and Tantra meditative practices, examining both the meditative states and the meditative traits. The study was carried out within the natural environment of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries in India, maintaining the socio-cultural context. Two groups of long-term practitioners (Buddhist monks of Gelug lineage), one experienced in the Tantra tradition (T-group, n = 21) and the other in the Sutra tradition (S-group, n = 20) participated in the study. A between-group cluster permutation test revealed that the groups differed in EEG alpha power during meditation, as well as in baseline resting conditions before and after meditation. Specifically, T-group demonstrated consistently lower alpha power compared to the S-group, regardless of the conditions. Thus, the observed differences are stable characteristics of the groups. The within-subjects analysis demonstrated that the conditions (meditation, and baseline resting states before and after meditation) differed only in the T-group: during meditation, an increase in individual alpha peak frequency (iAPF) was observed in the occipital leads, followed by a decrease in iAPF after meditation. We suggest that reported between-group differences represent enduring meditative traits developed through years of training in meditative techniques in the Sutra and Tantra traditions. Nevertheless, we cannot entirely exclude the possibility that these variations may also stem from certain cohort-specific characteristics unrelated to meditation. An examination of individual power spectra revealed that the absence of significant differences in EEG spectral power between conditions can be primarily attributed to the inter-individual variability in both groups. This variability, in turn, may stem from extensive expertise of highly experienced practitioners, who over years of training, develop individualized cognitive strategies for maintaining the meditative state. Our future research will focus on a more detailed quantitative analysis of inter-individual variability during meditations and on identifying additional between-group differences among practitioners in different traditions.

papers.title: Thalamic Reticular Nucleus Excitability and Cholinergic Signaling are Disrupted in a Mouse Model of Alzheimer's Disease Neuropathology.
papers.abstract: The thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) forms powerful GABAergic connections with thalamic nuclei that regulate sleep, attention, and sensory processing. TRN neurons receive dense cholinergic innervation from the basal forebrain and brainstem, dynamically shaping TRN function across brain states. We previously showed reduced TRN activity and sleep deficits in amyloid precursor protein transgenic mice (APP mice), implicating TRN dysfunction as an early contributor to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathophysiology. Here, using slice electrophysiology in mice of both sexes, we determined whether changes in intrinsic membrane properties or cholinergic synaptic transmission contribute to TRN hypoactivity in APP mice. We found that TRN neurons located in the inner core and outer shell regions undergo substantial increases in excitability after the first postnatal month. In mature animals, core neurons exhibited higher firing rates and diverse firing patterns, including persistent firing, whereas shell neurons fired at lower rates and displayed more homogeneous firing patterns without persistent activity. Firing diversity in core neurons was mediated in part by low-threshold T-type Ca²⁺ channels. Cholinergic synaptic activation, mediated predominantly by basal forebrain afferents, produced biphasic excitatory-inhibitory postsynaptic responses in both core and shell neurons, with the ratio of postsynaptic excitation and inhibition varying across postsynaptic targets. Overall, cholinergic activation suppressed TRN firing. In APP mice, core neurons showed reduced intrinsic excitability and cholinergic afferents evoked postsynaptic responses with a larger muscarinic receptor-mediated inhibitory component, leading to delayed TRN firing. Together, these findings identify both intrinsic and cholinergic synaptic mechanisms that may contribute to TRN dysfunction during early AD.Significance Statement Alzheimer's disease (AD) is typically diagnosed after cognitive symptoms emerge when treatments are less effective, highlighting the need to understand preclinical disease mechanisms. Cholinergic signaling and slow-wave sleep are disrupted before symptom onset, but the mechanisms underlying these changes remain poorly understood. Because the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) receives strong cholinergic input and mediates sleep-related rhythms, it is well positioned to contribute to early AD pathophysiology. We previously found reduced TRN activity and disrupted sleep in an AD mouse model. Here, we show that intrinsic excitability and cholinergic synaptic signaling are altered in TRN neurons during preclinical AD. These changes may contribute to thalamic dysfunction and sleep disturbances, providing a potential circuit mechanism linking early AD pathology to disease progression.

papers.title: Temporal Dynamics of Multi-Item Working Memory Maintenance in Human Gaze Patterns and EEG
papers.abstract: Maintaining multiple items in working memory (WM) requires the allocation of limited resources, which may involve prioritizing individual items over others. Previous work has suggested that attentional prioritization can vary rhythmically between WM samples, but direct empirical evidence for such temporal fluctuations remains scarce. Here, we recorded eye-tracking and EEG to track the temporal dynamics of multi-item processing while participants maintained up to three object orientations in WM. Whereas EEG encoding was only short-lived, miniature gaze patterns reflected the orientations of all three items throughout the entire WM delay and showed systematic load and serial position effects. Contrary to rhythmic sampling accounts, however, we found no evidence that eye movements alternated between the concurrently maintained items. Furthermore, the strength of WM encoding in gaze was not modulated by frontal theta activity in EEG, suggesting that oculomotor encoding was not directly coupled to rhythmic neural dynamics associated with WM and internal attention. Together, our findings indicate that the oculomotor signature of visuospatial WM processing was rather stably shaped by all of the simultaneously maintained items. The results further corroborate that eye-tracking and EEG provide complementary windows into the temporal dynamics of WM.

papers.title: Neural integration of musical and lyrical emotion: semantic-acoustic congruence in song processing.
papers.abstract: Songs convey emotion through the joint contribution of musical-acoustic structure, lyrical semantics, and vocal-prosodic expression, yet these information sources have often been examined separately in affective neuroscience. This Mini Review synthesizes behavioral, electroencephalographic/event-related potential (EEG/ERP), magnetoencephalographic (MEG), and functional neuroimaging evidence relevant to semantic-acoustic emotional congruence during song processing. Available findings suggest that lyrics and melodies engage partially dissociable but interacting processes during song perception. Early MEG responses around 130-140 ms differentiate lyric and melodic expectancy violations in memorized songs, while N400 modulations provide evidence of context-sensitive meaning-related processing across musical and verbal materials. Later positive components may reflect additional attentional allocation and evaluative processing under conflicting or ambiguous conditions, although their functional interpretations remain task-dependent. Functional neuroimaging studies have implicated superior temporal, middle temporal, and inferior frontal regions in lyric-melody processing, whereas studies of music-evoked emotion more broadly have reported activity in the amygdala, insula, cingulate cortex, hippocampus, and striatal regions. The specific contributions of these regions to music-lyric emotional congruence, however, remain uncertain. Behavioral evidence further suggests that congruence does not uniformly facilitate emotional processing and that incongruence may sometimes increase arousal or alter the relative weighting of musical and lyrical cues. On this basis, the review proposes a provisional dynamic weighted-integration account in which musical-acoustic affect, lyrical meaning, and vocal prosody interact across temporally overlapping processing stages, with their relative contributions varying according to expectations, attention, expertise, and language accessibility. Direct neural evidence specifically manipulating music-lyric emotional congruence remains limited, identifying an important direction for future naturalistic and multimodal research.

papers.abstract: To determine the frequency of epileptiform discharges (EPDs) in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) without clinical seizures, assess autism severity using the Childhood Autism Rating Scale, Second Edition (CARS-2), and reassess the children after treatment with antiseizure medications (ASMs). A prospective cohort study. Place and Duration of the Study: Four autism centres in Duhok City, Kurdistan Region, Iraq, from August 2024 to August 2025. Fifty children with seizure-free ASD (aged 2.5-18 years) underwent clinical evaluation, electroencephalography (EEG) recording, and severity assessment using CARS-2. Children with EPDs were offered ASMs according to EEG pattern and clinical profile. EEG and CARS-2 assessments were repeated after 6 months. Data were analysed using SPSS version 31.0. Descriptive statistics were presented as means ± standard deviations for continuous variables and frequencies with percentages for categorical variables. For group comparisons, independent t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests for small samples were used. A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. EPDs were detected in 24 participants (48%). EPDs were focal in 19 cases (79.16) and generalised in 5 cases (20.83). Adherence to ASMs after 6 months was observed in 9 cases (37.5 %). All adherent participants demonstrated EEG improvement and significant reductions in total CARS-2 scores (p = 0.001). Improvements were also observed in the following domains: emotional response (p = 0.023), body use (p = 0.024), activity level (p = 0.026), visual response (p = 0.040), taste, smell and touch (p = 0.057), and general impression of ASD (p = 0.026). Adverse effects were reported in 6/15 (40%) participants whom started ASMs, primarily behavioural. EPDs are common in children with ASD, even in the absence of clinical seizures. When ASMs were used consistently, EEG improvements were observed, and ASD severity scores on the CARS-2 were reduced. papers.title: A high-throughput all-optical platform for mapping gene perturbations to electrophysiology
papers.abstract: Electrical phenotyping remains a bottleneck in linking genes to cellular function. We developed a high-throughput all-optical electrophysiology platform combining an engineered human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) line, wide-field voltage imaging, and automated analysis. The hiPSC line integrates inducible NGN2, CRISPR interference, and degron-gated expression of Voltron2 and CheRiff, enabling neuronal differentiation, targeted gene knockdown, and optical electrophysiology. The microscope records approximately 1,500 spiking glutamatergic neurons at 800 Hz across a 4x4 mm field, with larger fields supporting approximately 3,000 neurons at 660 Hz. Automated analysis extracts single-cell voltage traces and quantifies firing patterns, action-potential waveforms, and subthreshold dynamics. Arrayed knockdown of five sodium- and potassium-channel genes produced distinct electrophysiological phenotypes. The engineered hiPSC line also supported optical electrophysiology recordings from motor neurons, astrocytes, and cardiomyocytes. These results establish a scalable platform for high-throughput electrophysiological phenotyping and functional genomics in hiPSC-derived cells.

papers.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Electroencephalography (EEG) detects clinical and subclinical seizures, but national utilization patterns remain poorly characterized. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Pediatric Health Information System (2016-2025) of neonates ≤28 days with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization. Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.

papers.title: Psychosis of Epilepsy: A Review of Diagnosis and Management.
papers.abstract: Neurology and psychiatry have been linked together for a long period of time. One overlap demonstrated in the literature is the correlation between epilepsy with mood and psychosis. There is a big group of psychoses called the psychosis of epilepsy (POE); however, there is not much evidence about the diagnosis and management. Differentiation between POEs is difficult and is compounded by a lack of evidence-based guidelines on appropriate management. Even if you arrive at the diagnosis, POE can be difficult to manage. Some antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) cause psychiatric side effects and some antipsychotics may be epileptogenic. In this poster, we will discuss ways to diagnose and treat POE, as well as how to optimize certain AEDs in patients with POE. Articles were chosen from multiple databases, such as MEDLINE, Google Scholar, and PsychInfo, to gather evidence about the diagnosis and management of POE. Specific keywords, such as Psychosis, Epilepsy, Antipsychotic, Antiepileptic, and Electroencephalogram (EEG) were used. Articles talking about recommendations regarding the use of AEDs and antipsychotics in POE were extracted from these databases. POE includes preictal, ictal, postictal, and interictal psychosis. Preictal psychosis is very rare and tends to present with dissociation and déjà vu. This is correlated with temporal lobe epilepsy and resolves after the seizure. Ictal psychosis will correspond with epileptic activity on EEG and can manifest as aggression, delusions, or hallucinations. Antipsychotics are contraindicated in this POE. Postictal psychosis usually presents as a combination of mood symptoms and grandiose delusions seen with interictal sharp epileptiform discharges on EEG. Interictal psychosis can be subtyped into brief and chronic, with brief occurring during periods of increasing seizure frequency and chronic having no association with seizures. They both present similar to symptoms seen in classic schizophrenia and antipsychotics are often utilized.Clozapine and chlorpromazine were found to have the highest seizure prevalence from second- and first-generation antipsychotics respectively, and the lowest was found with risperidone. AEDs that are commonly used in psychiatry, such as oxcarbazepine, carbamazepine, valproic acid, and lamotrigine are discussed in detail regarding their optimal dosing strategy for patients presenting with POE. Diagnosis and management of the various types of POE can be challenging due to the lack of literature. We recommend using the antipsychotic, risperidone, as it has shown to have the lowest seizure prevalence among all antipsychotics. Both neurologists and psychiatrists should keep POE on their differential when dealing with seizure patients with psychosis. It is crucial for psychiatrists to understand how to optimize AEDs in the management of POE as these patients are often seen on the consult service. No Funding.

papers.title: Aphasic status epilepticus presenting with prominent psychiatric symptoms: A case report.
papers.abstract: Aphasic status epilepticus (ASE) is a subtype of nonconvulsive status epilepticus characterized by aphasia as its primary ictal manifestation. Although psychiatric symptoms are uncommon in ASE, they may obscure the diagnosis when present. We report an atypical case, presenting predominantly with agitation and irritability, which was rapidly diagnosed as ASE by electroencephalography (EEG) based on the abrupt symptom onset and neurological history. A 49-year-old right-handed woman with alcohol use disorder was referred to our psychiatric hospital because of agitation, irritability, and disorganized thinking. Approximately 2 months before presentation to our hospital, she developed a generalized tonic-clonic seizure 3 days after sustaining a head injury. A left posterior fossa subdural hematoma was diagnosed, and burr-hole evacuation was performed at a general hospital. She continued rehabilitation; however, 6 days before admission to our hospital, she suddenly developed incoherent speech with agitation and irritability, prompting referral to our psychiatric hospital. Neurological examination revealed sensory aphasia. Given the history of brain injury and abrupt symptom onset, EEG was performed and demonstrated left-dominant periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges, confirming ASE. Antiseizure treatment resolved the EEG abnormalities and aphasia; however, aphasia, agitation, and irritability recurred with periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges. The symptoms improved with intravenous diazepam, and no recurrence was observed for >2 years following optimization of antiseizure medication. ASE may present predominantly with psychiatric symptoms and be misdiagnosed as a primary psychiatric disorder. Recognizing symptom chronology and epileptogenic background is essential for prompting EEG evaluation and early diagnosis.

papers.title: Rapidly progressive sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease overshadowed by a grief reaction and parkinsonism: a case report.
papers.abstract: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (sCJD) is a rapidly progressive and invariably fatal prion disease in which the first manifestations are psychiatric in a substantial proportion of cases. We report a 60-year-old man in whom sCJD was overshadowed both by a grief reaction and by a years-long presumed diagnosis of Parkinson's disease. Depressive, psychotic and cognitive symptoms that emerged after the loss of a close relative were initially interpreted as reactive, and an unexpected clinical deterioration followed the introduction of antidepressant and antipsychotic treatment. Electroencephalography showed periodic triphasic activity over the right frontotemporoparietal region, and diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated widespread bilateral diffusion restriction in cortical and deep grey matter. Autoimmune and paraneoplastic panels were negative, and a positive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) assay established a diagnosis of probable sCJD. The case underlines the importance of an organic differential diagnosis and of early multidisciplinary assessment in late-onset, rapidly progressive psychiatric presentations.

papers.title: Current strategies of cerebral oxygenation monitoring in general intensive care units: a narrative review.
papers.abstract: Cerebral hypoxia represents the final metabolic consequence of sustained intracranial pressure and impaired autoregulation. Continuous cerebral oxygen monitoring is essential to prevent secondary ischemic injury in neurocritical care particularly in severe traumatic brain injury, malignant infarction, and aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. It also guides management of systemic disturbances such as shock, sepsis, and respiratory failure and is increasingly used perioperatively in high-risk cardiac, carotid, and neurosurgical procedures. To synthesize physiological principles, monitoring modalities, and clinical applications of cerebral oxygenation across neurocritical care and perioperative settings, emphasizing bedside interpretation and integration within multimodal neuromonitoring. PubMed and Scopus were searched (January 2010-January 2025) using MeSH terms and keywords including "cerebral oxygenation," "brain tissue oxygen tension," "jugular bulb saturation," and "near-infrared spectroscopy." Fifty-eight English-language studies (randomized controlled trials, observational studies, reviews, and editorials) were included. Non-English publications, animal studies, conference abstracts, unavailable full texts, and non-peer-reviewed articles were excluded. Brain tissue oxygen tension, jugular bulb oximetry, and near-infrared spectroscopy provide complementary insights. Brain tissue oxygen tension is invasive and region-specific (<25 mmHg indicates high risk), jugular bulb oximetry reflects global cerebral oxygen extraction, and near-infrared spectroscopy enables noninvasive regional trend monitoring. Multimodal neuromonitoring integrating these with intracranial pressure, transcranial Doppler, and electroencephalography improves detection and management of secondary ischemia. In neurocritical care, invasive monitoring supports targeted interventions, whereas in ICU and perioperative settings, multimodal strategies balance diagnostic yield and feasibility. Cerebral oxygen monitoring should be routinely implemented in high-risk patients. Multimodal neuromonitoring should be prioritized to detect hypoxia early and guide individualized cerebral perfusion strategies. Near-infrared spectroscopy should be used for continuous monitoring, while invasive modalities should be reserved for high-risk neurocritical patients. Standardized thresholds and protocolized approaches should be established through prospective, outcome-driven research.

papers.title: International Survey of Stereo-EEG Practices: A Comparative Analysis of Epilepsy Surgery Centers in Europe and North America.
papers.abstract: Stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) is widely used for presurgical evaluation in epilepsy, yet practice patterns vary substantially across centers, contributing to heterogeneity in the literature. We examined differences in SEEG experience, techniques, and complications across Europe and North America centers. An electronic 39-item REDCap survey was distributed to centers participating in the American Stereo-EEG Consortium and EpiCARE Consortium. The survey assessed center characteristics, electrode planning and implantation, monitoring practices, and complications. Sixty-six centers responded, including 38 from North America and 28 from Europe. North American centers more frequently used nurse-led ictal and postictal assessments (16/38 vs. 5/28; P = 0.06) and robotic image-guided implantation systems (37/38 vs. 17/28; P < 0.001), with a trend toward higher case volumes. Compared with European centers, North American programs were less likely to have over 15 years of SEEG experience (6/38 vs. 12/28; P = 0.015), fewer dedicated SEEG readers (12/38 vs. 25/28; P < 0.001), and less frequent use of SEEG-guided radiofrequency ablation (13/38 vs. 25/28; P < 0.01). Symptomatic hemorrhage was more frequently reported among North American centers in the unadjusted analysis (9/38 vs. 1/28; p = 0.035); however, the regional difference was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for center SEEG experience and annual case volume. Significant differences exist between North American and European SEEG practices. North American centers more commonly use robotic implantation and manage higher volume, whereas European centers demonstrate greater experience and more frequent use of SEEG-guided ablation. These findings support the need for standardized protocols to improve safety and outcomes.

papers.title: Sex differences in cell type-specific transcriptional programs and GPCR signaling in the human subgenual anterior cingulate cortex
papers.abstract: Psychiatric conditions show marked sex differences in disease onset, symptom presentation, and response to treatments. Understanding how sex differences manifest across molecularly distinct neuronal populations in individuals without psychiatric conditions may help explain sex-dependent variation in neural circuit function and treatment response. Here, we examined molecularly distinct cell types within the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) of non-psychiatric subjects. Using RNA sequencing data previously generated from laser-capture microdissected neurons, we investigated sex differences in gene expression and co-expression networks in excitatory pyramidal neurons (layers 2/3 and 5/6) and somatostatin (SST)-, parvalbumin (PVALB)-, and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-expressing inhibitory interneurons (N=10 males, 9 females). We identified sex differences in transcriptomic profiles, biological pathways, and co-expression network connectivity. PVALB cells showed stronger overall female transcriptional enrichment, while SST cells exhibited male-enriched transcriptional signatures. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified PVALB and SST modules more connected in males and females, respectively, which included hub genes involved in immune, extracellular matrix, and bioenergetic processes. Since G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are viable therapeutic targets, we examined sex differences in GPCR transcripts. Across all GPCR-cell-type combinations, CHRM2 in PVALB cells showed the second strongest sex difference (enriched in females). To test the functional relevance of this difference, we used patch-clamp electrophysiology in mouse prefrontal cortex. M2 receptor activation increased maximal firing rates in PVALB cells from female but not male mice. Collectively, our findings demonstrate cell type-specific sex differences in the sgACC corresponding to functional differences in neuromodulator signaling, with potential implications for treatment response.

papers.title: Does Neurobiological Evidence Support the Diagnostic Distinction Between Hoarding Disorder and OCD? A Critical Narrative Review of Genetic, Neuroimaging, and Neuropsychological Findings.
papers.abstract: Hoarding symptoms were long regarded as one dimension of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), but DSM-5 (2013) classified hoarding disorder (HD) as a separate diagnosis. This review asks whether neurobiological evidence, including studies published after the reclassification, adequately supports that decision. This critical narrative review searched PubMed and Web of Science (January 2010 to July 2026, plus foundational studies found by citation tracing) and was structured according to the SANRA criteria. Genetic, neuroimaging, and neuropsychological evidence was judged against four questions: is hoarding a separable trait within OCD; do groups differ biologically on average; is any difference specific to hoarding; and can the evidence classify an individual patient? Twin studies suggest that hoarding-related traits have a heritability of about 26%-48%, and one genome-wide association study reported an SNP-based heritability of 11%. These estimates come from different models and are not directly comparable; they are compatible with a heritable, polygenic trait but do not by themselves show a disorder-specific genetic architecture. A small number of PET, structural MRI, functional MRI, and EEG studies report differences associated with hoarding, including seven direct HD-OCD comparisons, but samples are small, diagnostic criteria vary, and findings have not converged. An exploratory computational study has compared genetic signals for the two phenotypes, but no direct comparison of risk variants exists. Neuropsychological findings were inconsistent: the most recent systematic review found no significant impairment on most cognitive tests in HD. Current neurobiological evidence provides only supplementary, not definitive, support for the diagnostic distinction between HD and OCD. It points to group-level biological heterogeneity, but it does not establish a distinct etiology or individual-level diagnostic utility. Larger studies using standardized DSM-5 criteria and direct HD-OCD comparisons are needed.

papers.title: Macroscopic pulmonary fat embolism following cemented hemiarthroplasty for pathological femoral fracture: A case report with dual-energy CT spectral analysis.
papers.abstract: Macroscopic pulmonary fat embolism is an uncommon complication of cemented arthroplasty, and its occurrence after fixation of a pathological femoral fracture is rarely documented. We report the case of a 73-year-old woman with metastatic nonsmall cell lung cancer who developed severe hemodynamic instability during cement pressurization for hemiarthroplasty of a pathological right proximal femoral lesion, consistent with bone cement implantation syndrome but not fulfilling the criteria for fat embolism syndrome, and who recovered with supportive care. Dual-energy CT pulmonary angiography showed a 30 × 15 mm filling defect in the right main pulmonary artery and smaller left lower lobe segmental defects, with a mean attenuation of -86.6 HU within the main defect, CT numbers becoming progressively more negative at lower photon energies in contrast to a paraspinal muscle reference, and persistence of the defect on virtual noncontrast images. This case illustrates that attenuation measurement within any postoperative intraluminal filling defect is a simple and potentially decisive step, and that dual-energy spectral analysis may provide complementary support for the fatty nature of an embolus.

papers.title: Aluminum Foil Substrates Support Solvent-Free Raman Analysis of Skin Lipids.
papers.abstract: Sebum, a lipid-rich biofluid secreted onto the skin surface, holds promise as a non-invasive biomarker source but poses analytical challenges due to its hydrophobicity. Here, we demonstrate that aluminum foil substrates enable direct, solvent-free sampling and Raman spectroscopic analysis of human sebum, preserving key vibrational signatures of lipids, proteins, and carotenoids. We compared unprocessed sebum with chloroform/methanol and diethyl ether extraction methods in three volunteers, finding that solvent-free sampling yields more intense and chemically rich Raman spectra, while solvent-based methods attenuate signals and introduce compositional bias. Differential spectral analysis revealed that solvent extraction modifies the carbonyl and hydrocarbon stretching regions in a solvent-dependent manner. Our technical note focuses specifically on how sample processing affects the Raman spectral signature of sebum, underscoring the importance of solvent-free approaches and providing a methodological baseline for standardized Raman-based sebum analysis.
